exposure: pretreatment level of parent-rated child peer problems
outcome: post-intervention Children's Yale-Brown Obsessive-Compulsive Scale total score (CYBOCS)
cohort: The study included 72 children aged 11-18 years with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
finding: Higher baseline levels of parent-rated child peer problems strengthened the response to therapy for youth receiving TCBT, while family accommodation rated by mothers predicted poorer outcomes in both TCBT and CBT groups.
